en: This is the spirit of your dear father,
[Meaning uncertain: opening word unresolved.]
uncertainty_note: The opening word is unresolved; its initial resembles К rather than Н. The former interpretation as a proper name Nadishin and a claim of geographical origin are not established by the handwriting. Kyrgyz retained provisionally pending a defensible full reading.

en: His first ancestor was a khan,
He used to support him from the beginning [reading uncertain],
uncertainty_note: The overwritten first word remains provisional. The following words read колдоп жүрчү эле, rather than келген жүргүзүп эле; the object is implicit.

en: Kara Kozhal was of the Arabs,
Of the hero Booruk Kenen,
He was the one appointed,
Father Kalka became khan,
[Meaning uncertain: opening words unresolved.]
uncertainty_note: Opening words remain unresolved; neither the proposed Темик nor the interpretation involving laughter is secure. Kyrgyz retained provisionally; the previous fluent English was unsupported.

en: Making a people by Heaven's will,
Making the strength of his weapons,
Making the gathered clans a people,
Though oppressed, he grew mighty,
Multiplying from solitude,
Becoming the equal of the whole world,
Arstan Kozhal, the brave warrior,
Finding no mountain to dash against [reading uncertain],
uncertainty_note: The opening is provisionally read Урунарга; the internal joins remain indistinct. The former Үрүндө and English reference to an advance were unsupported.

en: Finding no enemy to wage war against,
Those people who heeded words,
He made into a people with his speech,
The fool who would not heed words,
He bent by force to his will,
No one had dared face him,
Saying, “Valiant Kenen, conquer!”,
He spared no enemy side,
The horse he rode was a bay charger,
Where the bay charger had not trotted or walked,
No land remained intact,
That Kenen did not demand and take,
No people remained intact,
That had not tried a cunning stratagem,
None of the cunning remained intact,
That Kyrgyz Kenen had not struck,
None among the peoples remained intact,
[Meaning uncertain: pale line unresolved.]
uncertainty_note: The pale line remains unresolved. Its ending may be өткүр шер rather than отур жер, so the former English about a central land where a sultan sits is not defensible. Kyrgyz retained provisionally; no speculative replacement adopted.

en: The foremost warrior born into the world,
Eloquent in speech, a wise man,
He granted whatever was wished,
He beat back the wrathful,
He reconciled what could not be reconciled,
Whatever anyone said to me,
He supplied an answer to them all,
Dust rose as though the earth had stirred,
A murmuring host came forth,
No man dared approach him face to face,
Narrow in temper, he would not open his hand,
The radiance never left his face.
Keeping companions, he gathered brave men,
From Tölögön's people he gathered his peers,

uncertainty_note: The first word appears to be Коң; the manuscript spelling is uncommon.
en: The land sustained their great chiefs,
Gathering the multitude, he cared for the people,
His thousand warriors who laid siege,
All those who had wandered,
Filling sacks with yellow gold,
Thinking deeply, he sustained the people,
Taking on the fury of a tiger,
He came to be called Kenen the Tiger,
Making the hero's arrow ready,
The enemy who poured out his wrath,
He destroyed him and drew blood,
No people remained to speak against him,
Saying, 'The mighty Kozhal has fallen,'
From his father to his forefathers,

uncertainty_note: The first word reads Казынадай, but its final suffix is visually uncertain.
en: Like a treasure upon his head,
Saying that fortune and prosperity had settled upon him,
The people spoke throughout the great realm,
Saying he had become the father of the people,
Whenever he seemed spent, he flared up anew,
He had grown strong from his very roots.
After each one died, in pursuit,
I myself led those who would strike them down,
uncertainty_note: The final word appears to be эрчиткен; the middle word may instead be кырлар.

en: [Uncertain: will they find the cart-load, frozen?]
uncertainty_note: All four word shapes are visible, but the phrase is not securely intelligible; арбан and балы may be different lexemes.

en: His heroism is great as well.
His own eyes saw it clearly,
The foremost sage,
Racing across the face of the earth,
He would emerge alone from the race,
His four racehorses were ready,
uncertainty_note: The first two words are pale and may have a different reading; күлүгү is inferred from the racing context.

en: From Saykal, whom the prince had taken,
uncertainty_note: The middle word is difficult; it resembles алган, while the final proper name reads Сайкалдан.

en: There was a soul who followed behind me.
Settling them on two summer pastures,
Was it the multitude that migrated?
uncertainty_note: The first word is a best-effort reading of a compressed cursive form; the line may instead contain көчүшкөн.

en: I lived in freedom,
Delighting the people, he went laughing,
uncertainty_note: жүрдү күлүп is the likely reading, but several letters overlap and are faint.

en: He had become the people's enclosure and refuge,
His heroism, his lionhearted courage,
Now it struck the palate like springtime,
uncertainty_note: The first two words remain unresolved at lexical level; this is a letter-shape transcription and the English is provisional.

en: If he roared fearsomely,
uncertainty_note: The final verb resembles чаңырса, but could be a closely related formula involving чаң.

en: His eyes reddening like a lion's,
[Uncertain: his mouth like a bow ...]
uncertainty_note: Жаадай and оозун are plausible; the final word is not securely deciphered and the line cannot be translated confidently.

en: Stretching out across the open steppe,
With a hundred close companions,
uncertainty_note: The possessive ending in жолдошуң and the numeral жүз are the likeliest readings, though both are cursively compressed.

en: His comrades were brave men,
[Uncertain: seething, equal in merriment,]
uncertainty_note: The line is fully visible but its second and third lexical forms are not secure; English follows the tentative reading.

en: When a black gun cracked,
Brave Kenen, who would not flee,
When a great gun boomed,
uncertainty_note: The first word is heavily cursive and may be another adjective; мылтык тарс этсе is clear.

en: Lionhearted Kenen would not startle and flee,
His majesty mounting, his wrath sharp,
uncertainty_note: This is a contextual normalization of difficult cursive; артып and курч are not fully secure on letter shape alone.

en: Noble Kenen, the gray-maned wolf,
[Uncertain: come as a somewhat superior equal,]
uncertainty_note: The final baseline is fully visible but remains lexically unresolved; this is the closest letter-shape reading.

en: His companions, growing calm,
uncertainty_note: The final word is a letter-shape reading; it may instead be жоолугуп or another жоо- form.

en: He lived as an equal among the people,
uncertainty_note: The first word is compressed and may be a different жүр- form; журтка тең болуп is clear.

en: Not sending the banners out on campaign,
uncertainty_note: The first and final words are plausible contextual readings of difficult cursive.

en: Not harming the people's neighbors,
uncertainty_note: The middle word resembles коңшусун but is not secure on letter shape alone.

en: Springing up and settling upon the bow,
uncertainty_note: The line is visible, but the first verb and the phrase's intended sense remain provisional.

en: His Kyrgyz people had lived in happiness,
uncertainty_note: Кыргызу is preserved as written; the final two words are faint and could contain a different auxiliary construction.

en: However much it might be so,
uncertainty_note: The first word is likely Канчалык, but its ending is tightly compressed.

en: Many people called him impartial,
uncertainty_note: Калыска is the closest visible reading, though калыс деп may be intended; English follows the apparent sense.

en: [Uncertain: the Kyrgyz people's fortune and honor,]
uncertainty_note: All word groups are visible, but даарын бак is not lexically secure and the translation is provisional.

en: He was called the middle Kulan,
uncertainty_note: Кулан appears to be a proper name; the first word could instead be a closely related form such as ортоңку.

en: Like a lake swelling over its banks,
The people were those who guarded it,
The Kyrgyz of Ala-Too,
The arrogant enemy who came saying, ‘I will take them,’
Was leveled with the black earth,
Setting his kinsmen's hearts at rest,
Of the tormenting oppressor,
Driving him off and breaking his back,
Saying, ‘It is an inheritance left by our fathers,’
Making Ala-Too their homeland,
[Uncertain: never sated in drinking his fill,]
uncertainty_note: The first word resembles Суран but is not securely intelligible; иче тойбогон is clearer.

en: Never abandoning his greed,
The dear Kyrgyz people in white felt caps,
If they met the enemy in combat,
uncertainty_note: Кармаша is preserved as the visible form; it may be an adverbial or a differently inflected verb.

en: He struck like a tiger,
uncertainty_note: The final verb appears to be сомдогон, though the contextual formula may use a similar-looking verb.

en: The people, an inheritance left by the fathers,
Making them a support fastened at his waist,
uncertainty_note: The phrase is a close letter-shape reading, but its morphology and exact idiomatic sense are uncertain.

en: The enemy who faced them was slaughtered,
uncertainty_note: The first word is clear in sense but several letters are compressed; союлуп is the likeliest final reading.

en: Saying, ‘May the people settle in good fortune,’
uncertainty_note: The middle and final phrase is faint; орносун таалай деп is a contextual reading.

en: Saying, ‘My Kenen remained for the people,’
uncertainty_note: The line clearly includes Журт and Кененим; the syntax and final verb are read provisionally.

en: Kenen was established as their support,
uncertainty_note: The final word appears to be коюлуп; арка may carry the idiomatic sense of protector or support.

en: [Uncertain: gathering around Kenen as their recourse,]
uncertainty_note: The final baseline is fully visible, but арга конушуп is not lexically secure; English is provisional.

en: The reason the people prospered,
The dear Kyrgyz people, countless in number,
Their errors passing, they became settled,
uncertainty_note: Ката is the closest letter-shape reading; the phrase may contain another lexeme.

en: In the time when none remained far away,
uncertainty_note: The first word appears to be Алыс, but its inner letters are pale; the translation is provisional.

en: The countless common people grew rich,
uncertainty_note: Сан кара is visually plausible and interpreted idiomatically as the mass of common people.

en: What had been broken was joined again,
The goods bestowed upon them were gathered,
uncertainty_note: The final word is compressed and may instead be жыйналат or a related form.

en: The growing hearths became known,
uncertainty_note: оттор and таанылып are best-effort readings of faint cursive; English follows those readings.

en: Where their cords were cut and birth-cloths washed,
The hills and open country, the laughing steppe,
uncertainty_note: The third and fourth words are difficult; талаа күлүш is a tentative letter-shape reading and the English is provisional.

en: Ala-Too became their inherited land,
They inhabited Ala-Too,
And became the white-capped Kyrgyz people,
The great one of the noble Kyrgyz,
The finest, to whom all turned their heads,
uncertainty_note: The middle word is read as бурушкан from context and letter shape; its ending is not fully secure.

en: A hero joined in spirit,
uncertainty_note: The final word resembles эрени; it may carry a different case ending.

en: Your young man was like a bow, his wrath fierce,
uncertainty_note: Жаадай and балаң are tentative readings of densely joined letters; the English is provisional.

en: The genial hero of many souls,
uncertainty_note: The line appears to read жайдары көп жан берени, but жан and берени remain lexically uncertain.

en: Kenen became a gray-maned hero,
Saying he was ready for every wish,
uncertainty_note: The grammatical ending in тилекке is normalized from a compressed form; белен is visually clear.

en: Saying, “Our hero is Kenen,”
uncertainty_note: Баатырбыз is the closest visual reading, although the inflection is contextually awkward and may differ.

en: Saying the Kyrgyz had bestowed good fortune,
uncertainty_note: The first word appears to be Таалайды, but several medial letters overlap.

en: Saying, “Kenen is our leader,”
All were enemies to the Kyrgyz,
Kenen, a hero steadfast as their stronghold,
uncertainty_note: Каттоосундай is a letter-shape transcription of an unresolved first word; the English gives only a contextual approximation.

en: Saying he stood ready for the enemy,
uncertainty_note: The middle word could be даяр or даар; даяр is adopted as the likely formula.

en: While this Kenen was among them,
If the hero went forth, the wind could not touch him,
uncertainty_note: Эр бүл is unresolved and may be a single word or proper name; the remainder reads жүрсө жел тийбей.

en: Yielding no challenge in the dark valley,
uncertainty_note: өзөнгө is visually plausible; the idiomatic force of доо бербей is translated provisionally.

en: A hero towering up to the clouds,
uncertainty_note: төбөй is the closest visual reading and may be a related verb meaning to rise or tower.

en: A hero who was the people’s protector,
His mount was a fierce falcon.
uncertainty_note: The final two words look like күр шумкар; this metaphorical description may conceal a horse name or different formula.

en: [Uncertain: the blind rootless one's roaming tread,]
uncertainty_note: The whole baseline is visible, but the first phrase and final noun are difficult cursive; this is a letter-shape reading and the English is provisional.

en: Nothing on earth remained intact,
Kenen drove them all onward,
No people remained intact,
The one he led was Ergey,
uncertainty_note: The proper name appears to read Эргей, but its medial letters are faint.

en: His sage, lofty Kögöy,
uncertainty_note: чок and the proper name Көгөй are plausible readings of compressed cursive; English follows that reading.

en: His close companion was that Boor,
uncertainty_note: The final proper name looks like Боор but is not secure; кошчусу is the likeliest reading of the middle word.

en: For the sake of a word about the mount,
uncertainty_note: All words are visible, but the phrase may contain a different first lexeme; translation is provisional.

en: Who inhabited Kara-Arka,
uncertainty_note: The first adjective appears to be Кара, though the place-name may be a nonstandard rendering of Сары-Арка.

en: Whom no man defeated in combat,
Who husked his millet, stones and all,
Who praised his wife as a maiden,
Who did not lie idle like his finest men,
uncertainty_note: The baseline is clear enough to segment, but the first word may have a different suffix; English is contextual.

en: [Uncertain: his own temper bristling,]
uncertainty_note: The middle noun and final verb are difficult; чаты бүркүрөп is a best-effort letter-shape reading.

en: Crying out what he himself had said,
uncertainty_note: The final word resembles чыркырап; the construction is not fully secure.

en: Who bound the top of the grave,
uncertainty_note: The visible phrase reads approximately Көр төбөнүн; its idiomatic sense is unresolved.

en: Who inhabited blue Sary-Arka,
uncertainty_note: Көк is visibly written before Сары Арка, but the resulting place epithet is unusual.

en: [Uncertain: no man defeated the one at the grave door,]
uncertainty_note: The first two words are a letter-shape reading and do not yield a secure phrase; адам жеңбеген is clear.

en: The dear people he thought of,
Who did not yield his ten arrows to another soul,
uncertainty_note: The opening may instead be a single word, оногун; read here as он огун from the visible spacing.

en: [Uncertain: the thrust spear remained blue,]
uncertainty_note: The opening participle is difficult and may not be шытыган; translation is strictly provisional.

en: Seventy peoples became fat,
uncertainty_note: The numeral and калкы are likely; the phrase's intended sense is uncertain.

en: The enemy who reached Kökö was laid low,
uncertainty_note: The first word looks like Көкө and may be a proper name or a different inflected form; жай болгон is translated contextually.

en: Warrior Orun, son of Ümötöy,
uncertainty_note: The final proper name appears to be Орун, but its last two letters are not fully secure.

en: This one's drove was excellent and splendid,
uncertainty_note: The phrase after айдагы is faint and lexically uncertain; мыкты соонун is a best-effort reading.

en: While this leopard Kenen was alive,
uncertainty_note: кабылан is contextually likely, though the medial letters are overwritten; the final word reads барында.

en: He struck the Kazakh people once,
He turned them back without letting them face him,
Thinking, Kök came at that moment,
uncertainty_note: окто and the final proper name Көк are uncertain; the verb келип is clear.

en: The labor Kökchö had borne,
uncertainty_note: The final noun appears to be эмгеги, though its initial vowel is lightly written.

en: [Uncertain: the restraint of the dear land,]
uncertainty_note: The final word resembles тыйы but is not a secure lexical reading; English is provisional.

en: [Uncertain: the side of his resentment, lofty barbar,]
uncertainty_note: This baseline is visible but lexically unresolved; Көкүн жагы чок барбар is the closest letter-shape transcription.

en: Of that land left under a curse.
To the north lay the Kor River,
uncertainty_note: The directional phrase Кутпа жагы is clear; the river name looks like Кор but may be a different short proper name.

en: Who inhabited the Lob River country,
The people wondered whether he would cease fighting,
uncertainty_note: The first two word shapes read Урушу койчубу, but the inflection and intended syntax are not fully secure.

en: No soul had turned his attention there,
uncertainty_note: The opening was overwritten by the scribe; Эч is supplied from the surviving letter traces and phrase context.

en: No living souls had gone there,
Who inhabited that land,
A land that living souls had never seen,
Who had fallen from a mountain like a bay horse,
uncertainty_note: The first word resembles Торудай and the final word resembles жыгылган; both are compressed and the simile is provisional.

en: Of the man who traveled by day,
uncertainty_note: Күндө is the likeliest reading of the opening word, though its second syllable is lightly written.

en: Whose daily fortune had been cut off,
uncertainty_note: The manuscript appears to separate Күн ырысы; the semantic rendering is provisional.

en: No solitary man had gone there,
uncertainty_note: The first word visibly resembles Жолон but may represent an uncommon or nonstandard form; English follows the apparent sense.

en: No solitary one remained alive,
uncertainty_note: As in the preceding line, Жолон is a letter-shape reading of an uncertain first word.

en: Its place was Kenen, its land secure,
uncertainty_note: Кенен may be the hero's name or an adjective meaning broad; the English preserves it as a proper name.

en: From his heart came a tale like this:
uncertainty_note: Боорунан is the closest reading of the opening word; the phrase could carry a more idiomatic sense.

en: An enemy warrior shaped like a man,
uncertainty_note: The line is legible, but its repeated киши construction is semantically unusual; translation is literal.

en: There, a man whose back was a mountain,
uncertainty_note: Айда is a best-effort reading of the first word; аркасы тоо киши is clearer and is rendered literally.

en: From where he inhabited the frozen wilderness,
uncertainty_note: The middle word looks like тоңоз but is not securely identifiable; English gives only the probable contextual sense.

en: The lone soul who went from captivity,
uncertainty_note: Каптан is the visible reading but may be a different ablative noun; translation is provisional.

en: Did not return alive without dying,
A man stronger than the Creator,
uncertainty_note: The final form looks like күчүүсү; the resulting hyperbolic comparison is translated literally.

en: No living man had gone there,
Surambek, khan of the Joygut,
uncertainty_note: Both Жойгут and the proper name Сурамбек are plausible readings of lightly written names, but neither is fully secure.

en: He struck him and drove him back once,
He turned him to face about and returned,
Bringing him safely from Tooz,
uncertainty_note: The final word reads approximately тооздон and may be a place name or a different common noun.

en: His heroism became known,
uncertainty_note: The first noun is compressed but most likely Берендиги, derived from берен.

en: From the gray-maned prince Kenen,
He made ready as of old,
His assumed name was found,
Was there one in the news of Kere?
uncertainty_note: The first two words appear to read Кере кабарында, but the phrase is lexically unresolved; English is deliberately literal and provisional.

en: Mounted for the mountains and took up his spear,
uncertainty_note: Тоого is the closest visible reading of the first word, though the construction минип with it is unusual.

en: At home a mace was fastened on,
uncertainty_note: The opening looks like Үйдө; the phrase is translated literally because its narrative relation is unclear.

en: He struck the one called Künchük,
uncertainty_note: The proper name Күнчүк and final verb are plausible readings of compressed cursive; translation is provisional.

en: He turned one back to face him,
Striking Künchük, he took him home,
uncertainty_note: The proper name and үйдө are the likeliest readings, but both are cursively compressed.

en: Destroying the grave, he took the encampment,
uncertainty_note: Көрдү is a letter-shape reading and may be another object; English follows it provisionally.

en: Taking a thousand to load the baggage,
Taking the host forward on its march,
uncertainty_note: The first and third words appear to be Алга and дүйнө, but the phrase is semantically uncertain.

en: Oylok, with fawn-like eyes,
uncertainty_note: Ойлок may be a proper name; the middle word is especially difficult and the idiomatic English is conjectural.

en: The dark-eyed one he had in mind,
Would he speak of the crimson dress?
uncertainty_note: The last word looks like айтабы; its connection to the preceding noun phrase is uncertain.

en: He seized and tore away their possessions,
uncertainty_note: The first noun is a difficult cursive reading; English gives only the apparent action.

en: Throwing them into distress, he raged,
uncertainty_note: Бейпай and бүркүргөн are plausible letter-shape readings; translation is provisional.

en: He turned one back to face him,
The hero's heroic strength became known,
uncertainty_note: The third word appears to be жени but may represent a different lexeme; English takes it as strength.

en: No enemy could remain before his advance,
Nothing remained in the treasury to give,
Those who saw this lost heart,
uncertainty_note: The final phrase is clearly shaped but its exact idiomatic force is uncertain; English renders the apparent sense.

en: Saying, 'This ill-omened Kenen,'
Saying, 'This is the bloodthirsty hero's son,'
Despairing before his power,
uncertainty_note: укумунан is a literal letter-shape reading and may stand for a related word meaning power or force.

en: His charge left them wounded,
uncertainty_note: Both long words are difficult; the reading and English are provisional.

en: They cried out before him,
uncertainty_note: The middle and final words are compressed and overwritten; this is a best-effort contextual reading.

en: If you observe him, this Kenen is formidable,
uncertainty_note: байкасаң is the likeliest reading of faint cursive; the rest is comparatively clear.

raw: Бу кез болуп адам барбайт деп,
en: Saying, 'No man will go and face him,'
uncertainty_note: кез болуп is a tentative segmentation of the cursive phrase; English follows the broader context.
text: Бу кез болуп адам барбайт деп,

raw: Буга кез болгон туруп калбайт деп,
en: Saying, 'Whoever meets him will not remain standing,'
uncertainty_note: The phrase кез болгон is tentative, though the sense of the line is reasonably clear.
text: Буга кез болгон туруп калбайт деп,

en: Those who fought him fell back defeated,
uncertainty_note: The last two words are difficult cursive; English conveys the apparent defeat formula.

en: Saying, 'There is no strength to make him yield,'
uncertainty_note: Боо бербешин is a tentative reading of an idiomatic phrase; translation is contextual.

en: To his right lay the Russian people,
They thought, 'So this is Kenen,'
His might was as fierce as China's wrath,
uncertainty_note: The final phrase is overwritten and may contain a different noun or adjective; English is provisional.

en: Saying, 'If you grapple with him, ready your life,'
uncertainty_note: The middle of the line has a struck-out correction; жаның белен is the clearest surviving reading.

en: So the Russian people thought,
Before them stood a firearm,
uncertainty_note: бараң appears to be the archaic word for a firearm, but the referent and syntax remain uncertain.

en: These wretched ones were of the Kyrgyz tribe,
uncertainty_note: The baseline is clear overall, but байкуш and the final case ending are difficult cursive readings.

en: Intending to overrun and oppress them,
uncertainty_note: кысмак is a contextual reading of tightly joined letters; the English is provisional.

en: A countless host gathered from the rich lords,
uncertainty_note: The first word appears to be Байдан, but its internal consonant and the phrase's sense are not secure.

en: They came saying, “We will wage war,”
Barak's banner was brought down,
uncertainty_note: The proper name Барак and possessive ending are plausible but compressed in the manuscript.

en: With Ebegey and Kögöy there as well,
uncertainty_note: The two proper names are legible with help from the parallel printed witness; the opening word is faint.

en: Kenen became lord over these Kyrgyz,
This assembled army was scattered,
This hero's people were subdued,
uncertainty_note: эрендин is the likeliest reading of the middle word, whose initial letters are lightly written.

en: The people of this foe faltered,
uncertainty_note: догонун is a letter-shape reading of an unclear lexeme; translation follows the hostile context.

en: Those Kalmyk souls who said they would do battle,
uncertainty_note: катташам is plausible from context and letter forms, but its medial cluster is difficult.

en: Those fierce warriors who would wage holy war,
uncertainty_note: The words казат and албууттар fit the visible strokes and context, but both are heavily joined.

en: Their great stronghold was cut down,
uncertainty_note: чымбары is an unresolved manuscript lexeme; transcription and contextual English are provisional.

en: Their great ambition was checked,
uncertainty_note: The final verb may instead be a closely related form such as тынган; the visible strokes favor тыйылган.

en: No one remained to answer him defiantly,
No force remained that could overwhelm him,
Dear Kenen became khan,
And wherever he looked was at peace,
His honor was high and his wrath was mighty,
He split a black hair with perfect justice,
Between kin and enemy,
He never tore them apart or divided them unjustly,
He never favored the wicked,
He arose as a blessed lion,
Generous in nature and broad of heart,
His fortune was perfectly fulfilled,
Splitting a black hair with perfect justice,
He arose as an impartial warrior-sultan,
The envious burned with resentment,
And his many watchful enemies,
Without even fighting, despaired of life,
His name became known throughout the world,
While gray-wolf Kenen reigned,
His chief wife Gulayym,
Saw her affairs blossom like flowers,
And her fortune surged and overflowed,
Named Kulansaryk and Alymsaryk,
She bore two sons,
When she had given birth to them,
Their forefather was Khan Tugan,
uncertainty_note: The proper name Туган is a close reading of the joined medial letters and is absent from the nearby abridged printed witness.

en: From the beginning, the line had continued one by one,
uncertainty_note: жалгыздан is visually likely, but the final morphology and implied lineage sense remain provisional.

en: She said, “I have borne two sons,”
“My wings now span a fathom, my tail fills an embrace,”
“I have taken my place among the people,”
There was no regret in what she had received,
uncertainty_note: Алган is the likeliest opening word, but the phrase is compressed and the English is contextual.

en: One of the seven days brings death,
For God will take every person,
The cold-bosomed black earth,
Will one day open its embrace,
A soul is but a guest for seven days,
And will return when its turn comes,
The cold-bosomed black earth,
Will one day draw us to its bosom,
No person has a breast of iron,
uncertainty_note: көөдөн is a contextual reading of a heavily joined word; the visible letter forms do not make every vowel secure.

en: Even a cherished noble soul,
uncertainty_note: Ардактаган is the most plausible reading of the lightly written opening word.

en: Will return when the children come of age,
uncertainty_note: жете is visually plausible, but the idiom and its relationship to кайтар are uncertain.

en: Her platter-round face brightened,
Thinking her dear sister-in-law would take them,
uncertainty_note: балдыз is a difficult cursive reading and the object of алар is implicit; the English remains provisional.

en: The deep-rooted black earth,
Will one day open its embrace,
My Alym and my Kulan.
My young heroes whom I beheld with joy,
Thinking, “These two will remain after me,”
She cherished them as her support and devoted herself to them,
For the children she had borne,
She implored that they be her heirs,
Stirring the people and gathering the nation,
uncertainty_note: The opening phrase is a best-effort reading of lightly written, joined cursive; дүрбөтүп is contextually plausible but not fully secure.

en: Those who did not hold back rejoiced,
uncertainty_note: Карбайгандар is the closest visible reading, but the lexeme and therefore the English are provisional.

en: His honor, fortune, and prosperity,
uncertainty_note: The three-noun reading fits the visible letter groups, though the middle word and inflection are faint.

en: Became known to the multitude,
Such was the hero Kenen,
The four kinds of livestock stood ready,
uncertainty_note: The manuscript appears to compress the phrase as төрт түлүгү белен экен; the last two words are lightly formed and the English is contextual.

en: He had ninety animals slaughtered for the feast,
He had the children cradled and cherished,
And gave them rhyming names,
He became a man of surpassing prosperity,
He stood like a bannered, mist-crowned mountain,
At the feast for those two,
A clamor arose that split the sky,
May God never let us see such a sight,
The multitude standing there came to a halt,
uncertainty_note: Токтоп is the likeliest reading of the first word; its internal letters are faint.

en: An ancestral household that would never be exhausted,
uncertainty_note: The first two words are fairly clear, but the closing phrase resembles мураа үй and remains unresolved; the English is provisional.

en: People filled the face of the earth,
They held the feast for seven days,
At that very feast,
All whom ears had heard of and eyes had seen,
Every living soul gathered,
The warrior restrained the fierce ones,
uncertainty_note: This manuscript-only line is faint. Азууларын эр кайтарган is a letter-shape reading; both syntax and English remain provisional.

en: It made the lower-ranking men rejoice,
uncertainty_note: The line appears to read Астынкы эрдин шаңдаткан, but the final verb is heavily joined and may be another related form.

en: It made those in the encampment crane their necks proudly,
uncertainty_note: The baseline is fully visible but pale. Ордодогу and the idiomatic койкоңдоткон are best-effort readings; the middle word and translation are provisional.

en: Its two humps rose prominently,
Dust covered its forehead,
uncertainty_note: The phrase is contextually clear, but the middle letters of Маңдайынан are lightly and tightly written.

en: It planted all four feet evenly,
Dust covered its shaggy hair,
The black camel glared fiercely,
uncertainty_note: The final word looks like нар and suits the camel description; the compressed letters could admit another reading.

en: The camel, lord among livestock,
Looking like a thoroughbred camel,
uncertainty_note: A crossed-out word precedes the retained baseline; аргымак is the best reading of the replacement phrase.

en: He had all of it loaded onto camels,
uncertainty_note: The manuscript appears to read Нардан; the case form and resulting English are provisional.

en: He held equestrian entertainments,
uncertainty_note: The final verb is faint; өткөрдү is the best contextual reading.

en: Having the black load piled on,
uncertainty_note: мөңгү is a tentative letter-shape reading of an unresolved word; the English is only contextual.

en: They say he held a great feast,
Seeking a means to beguile them,
uncertainty_note: The short line is pale; Алдоону издеген is a best-effort reading and its connection to the feast passage is unclear.

en: Livestock gathered in countless numbers,
uncertainty_note: күтүрүп is the likeliest reading of the joined medial letters; the idiomatic English is provisional.

en: For the people who remained alive,
Their hearts were truly put at ease,
Two treasures' worth of white sheep,
uncertainty_note: The line visually reads Эки казына ак койдун, but the construction is unusual and the English remains literal.

en: Having their lambs slaughtered,
Leaving their mothers in the dark,
uncertainty_note: караң контуруп is an unresolved reading of strongly joined handwriting; the English is a literal provisional rendering.

en: Precious goods were gathered among them,
uncertainty_note: ара is the visible reading, but the phrase may contain a different word division; translation is contextual.

en: Slaughtering mares amid the bustle,
uncertainty_note: The first word appears to be Кайнаган, though its relation to бээ is semantically uncertain.

en: For it, slaughtering three hump-backed camels,
uncertainty_note: The line appears to repeat үч around өркөчүн; both transcription and syntax are uncertain.

en: The dark livestock of all four kinds,
Slaughtering equally from all four kinds of livestock,
Yellow gold piled in abundance,
uncertainty_note: Капкалаган is a tentative reading of a corrected and overwritten word; the English conveys the apparent sense.

en: They say he proclaimed its worth imploringly,
uncertainty_note: кымын is an unresolved manuscript lexeme and may be a different word; the English is highly provisional.

en: Today, countless livestock for the household,
uncertainty_note: үйкөө is a best-effort reading of an unclear word; syntax and English are provisional.

en: They say he scattered its share lavishly,
uncertainty_note: кымын remains unresolved as on line 25; English follows the apparent distribution context.

en: Of every person who came,
They say he attended even to the last of them,
uncertainty_note: басыптыр is visually likely, but the idiomatic sense in this passage is uncertain.

en: For all of them, and for the poor,
uncertainty_note: The opening word is faint but appears to be Баары; this final baseline continues syntactically onto the next page.

en: To orphans and widows,
To the aged and the weak,
uncertainty_note: Карган is the best visual reading; it appears to mean aged people here, though the form may be nonstandard or abbreviated.

en: To the weak who kept no livestock,
All the yellow gold and property,
uncertainty_note: мүлктүн is a contextual reading of tightly joined handwriting; the final word clearly reads баарысын.

en: Calling them with earnest entreaty,
uncertainty_note: The opening word appears to be Зарын, but the phrase is idiomatically uncertain.

en: The six-branched haunch,
uncertainty_note: айрыны жамбашты is the closest letter-shape reading; the livestock or feast expression and English remain unresolved.

en: Having the marksmen shoot,
Cattle, horses, and dark livestock,
Females and males mixed together,
After slaughtering them for the grand festivities,
uncertainty_note: The first phrase looks like Таң тамаша; it may represent the conventional expression таң-тамаша.

en: He immersed them in great merriment,
uncertainty_note: The final verb appears to be баткызат; tense and exact idiomatic force are provisional.

en: The larger yearlings and calves,
Having them presented to the young men,
He slaughtered many for the prizes,
uncertainty_note: сан is visually likely and is rendered as many; the compact phrase may carry a specialized feast sense.

en: For this he made them surpass the whole people,
uncertainty_note: The manuscript reads Бул үчүн; the referent and the precise sense of арттырып are context-dependent.

en: A two-year-old heifer,
Letting its hair-tail grow,
Having the girls remove the hair,
uncertainty_note: кыл жойтуп is the best visual reading, but the described custom and therefore the English are uncertain.

en: Having it paced through the winter,
uncertainty_note: Кыштырата is a tentative reading of the underlined first word; жордуруп is clearer.

en: Having the prizes staked,
Having them set out in a long procession,
uncertainty_note: Чубайууга is the visible form; its specialized racing sense is uncertain.

en: The three-year-old horse,
Having them race in order,
What they called a three-year-old and a four-year-old,
uncertainty_note: The age-class words are legible, but the syntax is compressed; бышты and кунан denote horse age classes.

en: Having each bear its allotted lot,
uncertainty_note: жазасын literally suggests punishment or fate; in this racing context the English is provisional.

en: The one that performed best of all,
The female that received the award,
uncertainty_note: Угаган is an unresolved letter-shape reading; тийген ургаачы is clearer. The English follows the prize context.

en: The one called a three-year-old or four-year-old,
uncertainty_note: The age-class terms are visible, but their grammatical relation to the surrounding lines is uncertain.

en: The people gathered to see it,
uncertainty_note: The baseline is fully visible but the middle word looks like козуго and is lexically unresolved; the English is contextual.

en: They gathered the groups together,
uncertainty_note: Both оролорду and чор кокту are tentative letter-shape readings of a difficult line; the English only conveys the apparent collective action.

en: Having its award placed into their hands,
uncertainty_note: The words are visually clear, but жазасын is rendered as award from the racing context rather than its usual sense punishment; the sentence continues on the next page.

en: Zaitaker, at last, to Bishkek,
uncertainty_note: The first word appears to be the proper name Зайтакер; the syntax and reading of соңку are provisional.

en: Having it stated plainly and shown,
uncertainty_note: The overwritten opening word is best read Таасын; its first medial letters remain obscured.

en: If wronged, he drew blood,
uncertainty_note: Кара кылса is the best visual reading, but the idiom and translation are provisional.

en: His just-born Kyzyr,
uncertainty_note: The final name looks like Кызырын, but its ending is compressed and may be inflectional.

en: A five-year-old horse as the feast's prize,
uncertainty_note: Бышты and байгесин are visually likely; the elliptical relation between them remains provisional.

en: Having a heifer brought and given,
For his campaign before the people,
uncertainty_note: The last word is faint and provisionally read жортуна; translation follows that reading.

en: Making it known that he was a hero.
Twins were born among all the people,
Saying, “Among twins there have never been such as these,”
They made it the heart of their talk,
uncertainty_note: Өзөк is visually plausible, though the first word's medial letters are lightly written.

en: Those who disparaged them spoke that way,
uncertainty_note: The line is legible as written, but андай may instead be a similarly shaped demonstrative and the English is contextual.

en: A person who said, “Such as these,”
uncertainty_note: мындан is the best reading of the faint central word; the phrase is elliptical.

en: Saying, “Among twins there will not be two like them,”

raw: Баатыр да ушул, эр да ушул,
en: This one is the champion; this one is the hero,
uncertainty_note: The opening word is overwritten but context and visible letter shapes support Баатыр.
text: Баатыр да ушул, эр да ушул,

en: Born in a time of abundance,
Born to bring accord,
uncertainty_note: салган is the likeliest reading of the joined central word; translation is contextual.

en: Saying, “This is the summit of abundance,”
uncertainty_note: The final noun appears to be чокусу; the comparative construction is provisional.

en: Striving like Kara-Köz,
uncertainty_note: The opening word and the proper-name reading Кара Көз are tentative; the manuscript joins are faint.

en: Of the Shibe and the Targoot,
uncertainty_note: The second ethnonym is provisionally normalized as Таргоот from faint handwriting.

en: Of the Manchu and the Solon,
Of the Shibe and the Black Kalmak,
Among the Yellow Chinese in Kakan,
A thousand black beasts were brought down,
uncertainty_note: The line visually reads миң кара, but the livestock noun is elliptical and the English supplies the contextual referent.

en: Abundant livestock were slaughtered for the feast,
Honored by the young men,
uncertainty_note: The ending балдардан is visually likely, but the case relation and English remain provisional.

en: Having them set in fitting order,
uncertainty_note: Арын уйкаш is a best-effort reading of pale, joined handwriting; translation conveys only the apparent ordering sense.

en: All of the khans ate their fill,
Black livestock from every valley were slaughtered for the feast,
uncertainty_note: Сай кара is visually clear but elliptical; livestock is supplied contextually in English.

en: People of many kinds came,
People came from every tribe without exception,
Making dwellings across the lowlands,
uncertainty_note: ойкулдан is a tentative reading of the faint central word; translation is contextual.

en: A festive people gathered,
uncertainty_note: The final word looks like туулган, though the feast context may imply a different verb; English is contextual.

en: The great multitude rose in a roar,
uncertainty_note: The short final line is pale; дуу болуп is the best contextual reading and continues syntactically onto the next page.

en: When his Kalatai stood complete,
uncertainty_note: Калатайын is the best visual reading; the proper name or lexeme is not securely identified, so the English transliterates it.

en: His Kozakbai, who remained among them,
uncertainty_note: The joined middle and final letters are faint; Козакбайын is a provisional proper-name reading.

en: When the disturbance had passed in such a way,
uncertainty_note: The first word appears to be бүлөөн, an uncertain dialectal or manuscript form; translation is contextual.

en: The horses grew fat and sleek,
The men grew eager, pent up inside,
uncertainty_note: Элигип and бук are visually plausible but the idiom is unresolved; English is provisional.

en: The mouth of the treasury opened,
uncertainty_note: Казыка is the best reading of the first word, but its sense here is unclear; translation follows the wealth-distribution context.

en: Much wealth was scattered,
It was strewn among those who would consume it,
uncertainty_note: Жейпесерге is a difficult joined reading and may contain a different beneficiary noun; English is literal and provisional.

en: Tying a gray sack for the allotment,
uncertainty_note: Ойлоо and the resulting phrase are uncertain; боз байлап is clearer.

en: They seized the splendid goods among themselves,
uncertainty_note: The first word most closely resembles Айбынды, though the noun it qualifies is implicit.

en: The wealth that lay in the lowland,
They sold it to those who were there,
uncertainty_note: сатышып is the best visual reading, though таратышып may be expected contextually.

en: They loaded it according to their strength,
uncertainty_note: The ending is compressed; артышып is the best reading and translation remains contextual.

en: They had divided it while the day still lasted,
His thought was on the host at the feast,
uncertainty_note: The final word appears as чериге; syntax and translation are provisional.

en: For Chymayym's sake,
uncertainty_note: Чымайымдын is a provisional proper-name reading.

en: For you yourself and for the khan,
uncertainty_note: The grammatical form өзүңдү is visually plausible but may represent another possessive form.

en: The wolf's blood—Khan Tengir,
uncertainty_note: A word is struck through before the retained name Хан Теңир; Бөрүнүн каны is the best reading of the uncrossed text.

en: A descendant of Khan Kongurbai,
The one who arose from his lineage,
uncertainty_note: Урайынан is the best visual reading; it is interpreted as lineage here.

en: The shoot that sprang from his root,
uncertainty_note: Both words are tightly joined and pale; reading and figurative translation are provisional.

en: A mighty one from his stock,
uncertainty_note: This is a low-confidence reading of a faint baseline; English gives only the apparent genealogical sense.

en: The heir of Chunka Khan,
uncertainty_note: Чуңка and тоорасы are best-effort readings; heir is a contextual rendering of the unresolved final noun.

en: The noble lord of Kalkan,
uncertainty_note: Калкандын could alternatively be калкымдын; the place or collective reference is unresolved.

en: Counted among the forty Kyrgyz tribes,
His keen one clad in chased armor,
uncertainty_note: The final word is especially faint and is transcribed provisionally as кырчылгы.

en: His pure champion who girded on stone-hard armor,
uncertainty_note: сайынган is visually likely; the martial English sense is contextual.

en: The warrior arrayed for the bazaar,
uncertainty_note: The line is pale; Базарга кийген is the closest reading, but the formula may be different.

en: Terrible to behold, full of venom,
uncertainty_note: The first two words are faint and compressed; translation follows the clearer заары көп.

en: A hero known to the people,
Whom no outsider had ever seen,
A living radiance stood upon his face,
A wondrous one, with venom of another kind,
uncertainty_note: Таңкулуу башка is a low-confidence reading of pale connected script; English is provisional.

en: He was a fearsome khan who mounted the throne,
uncertainty_note: так is read as throne; the manuscript spacing permits айбаттак as a single unclear form.

en: The land filled with the forty Kyrgyz tribes,
uncertainty_note: The third word is clearly кыргыз; тулган is a provisional reading of the following pale word.

en: Would he come forth from Kongur...
uncertainty_note: The final baseline is pale, ends incompletely, and continues onto the next manuscript page; чыгабы is the best reading.

en: He was a man who stood like a dark falcon.
uncertainty_note: The faint opening word is provisionally read Чуңкара; the line continues the description from folio 402.

en: His majesty was like tempered steel,
uncertainty_note: The short middle word appears to be ок; English renders the simile contextually.

en: Among the mortals born in this world,
uncertainty_note: The final word is faint and provisionally read ушунда.

en: There was no scourge greater than he.
uncertainty_note: The first word looks like Дажалы and is translated in its figurative sense; the comparison particle is faint.

en: The child of turmoil, Tokson Khan,
uncertainty_note: The phrase Бал бүлүкү and the name Токсон are provisional readings of joined handwriting.

en: He would send word throughout the world,
Of those who chose, this one was foremost,
uncertainty_note: Талгочудан is the best visual reading but the lexeme and resulting English remain provisional.

en: The worthy words I would speak,
He expressed openly and precisely,
He praised what he had conceived,
uncertainty_note: The final word is faint and provisionally read мактоочу.

en: Seeing an enemy, he would mount his horse,
A tiger-hearted man, unmatched in turmoil,
uncertainty_note: The final phrase is visually difficult; жок бүлүк is retained provisionally and translated contextually.

en: When Kyrgai attacked as he came into view,
uncertainty_note: Келе көргүндө and the proper name Кыргай are provisional readings.

en: That was what Kyrgai found,
uncertainty_note: The middle name and final verb are faint; this reading follows the apparent repetition from line 13.

en: Surun Khan, who came from the Kyrgyz,
uncertainty_note: The proper name is heavily overwritten and provisionally read Сурун.

en: No soul could tire of his fine bearing,
At the khan's majesty, hearts took courage,
uncertainty_note: The ending appears to be жүрөк түр, but spacing and grammar are uncertain; English is contextual.

en: Saying, 'The eagle does not shrink back,'
uncertainty_note: The joined middle phrase бүрбөй курай is difficult and may represent different words; translation is provisional.

en: He made his renown visible to the Chinese,
uncertainty_note: The middle noun is provisionally read дүңгү; English follows the apparent sense of fame or commotion.

en: Among the Chinese he became a lofty figure,
The wrathful hero Khan Tengir,
Thinking a prudent thought,
uncertainty_note: The second word appears to be иймен but the intended form and nuance are unresolved.

en: He was skilled at finding stratagems,
By making inquiries, he found a people,
The khan heeded the words of the inquiry,
uncertainty_note: The opening phrase and syntax are faint; Суруудан кебине is a provisional reading.

en: He became a rumor among the Chinese,
uncertainty_note: Ушук is the best visual reading and is interpreted as a report or rumor.

en: That one who went from the Kyrgyz,
To the young champion of the in-laws,
uncertainty_note: The middle word resembles сөөт but is unresolved; the translation is contextual and provisional.

en: They mounted him on an unbeatable pacer,
They dressed him in silk no bullet could pierce,
Among the Chinese people of twenty khans,
uncertainty_note: The relation of эли and Кытайда is syntactically uncertain, though the individual words are visually plausible.

en: Making it known with a smiling face,
uncertainty_note: The first two words are faint and provisionally segmented as Жылмай жүзгө.

en: He had seen the brave men boast,
uncertainty_note: The middle verb is provisionally read какап; its sense is inferred from context.

en: The two reins and a single lead-rope,
uncertainty_note: The final faint baseline is provisionally read as the common formula Эки тизгин бир чылбыр and continues onto the next page.

en: In Suurgan's time, it was bestowed.
uncertainty_note: The faint opening proper name and final verb are best visual readings; the sentence continues the preceding page's genealogy.

en: Making the Blue Dörböt into a people,
He brought turmoil upon the Kalmyks,
The reins of all Beijing,
He received from Tüp Teñir,
uncertainty_note: Түп Теңир is a visually plausible title or proper name; it may instead be a compressed epithet.

en: He took it from the people by the armful.
uncertainty_note: The first two words are faint and joined; transcription and idiomatic English are provisional.

en: Calling Suurgan the great Blue Khan,
uncertainty_note: кама is the best visual reading but the title is unresolved; English renders it contextually as 'great.'

en: Calling him a singular, contented soul,
uncertainty_note: жөрөлгөн is a provisional reading of a faint joined word; translation follows the apparent sense.

en: He ruled with surpassing authority,
The khans who spoke at one time,
uncertainty_note: The middle phrase is pale; учурда айткан is the best visual segmentation.

en: He slaughtered several of them.
Seeing his awesome might, Tüp Teñir,
uncertainty_note: The final name or title is the same provisional reading as line 5.

en: Gave it to his Kalmyk people,
uncertainty_note: Калмаканына is an uncertain manuscript form; English is contextual.

en: Placing the Ayran crown upon him,
uncertainty_note: Айран is the best visual reading of the modifier before таажысын but its referent is unresolved.

en: Carefully seating him upon the throne,
uncertainty_note: The first verb is pale and provisionally read as Изилдеп.

en: Giving him a beard and mastery,
uncertainty_note: ээ is visually plausible; the formula and its English sense remain provisional.

en: His land for a day, his day for the world,
uncertainty_note: Both halves are faint and the idiom is unresolved; transcription and literal English are provisional.

en: Giving night to his due,
uncertainty_note: The opening noun and the formula are unresolved; English is deliberately literal.

en: Seating the remaining one on the throne,
uncertainty_note: The first word is pale and could be a proper name or title rather than калган.

en: Giving him rule over the khagan's people,
Saying his spiritual power reached afar,
Frightening all of Beijing,
The Kalmyk called Azyrky,
uncertainty_note: Азыркы may be a proper name, an epithet, or the ordinary adjective 'present'; English preserves it as a name.

en: Putting the Jan cap upon him,
uncertainty_note: Жан is a provisional modifier or name; the act of placing a cap is clear.

en: Wherever he went, did he not act as a governor?
uncertainty_note: The final word is faint; калдай is interpreted as the title 'governor.'

en: Was he not the one called Cold-Tongued?
uncertainty_note: The internal punctuation and final auxiliary are inferred from a faint, joined line; translation is contextual.

en: A sixty-headed dragon,
The women beneath him,
uncertainty_note: The second word is a best visual reading of very pale handwriting; English is literal.

en: From the weary black treasure,
uncertainty_note: Both тажайган and казынан are provisional readings; the phrase's meaning is unresolved.

en: His true nature from himself,
uncertainty_note: The middle word is faint and semantically unresolved; English follows the apparent syntax.

en: He had Khan Suurgan taught,
He held his white standard,
uncertainty_note: түңгөрүн is a provisional reading of a faint lexeme; 'standard' is contextual.

en: A Chinese soul studied here,
uncertainty_note: жан мында is the best visual segmentation; the construction and English are provisional.

en: The khan gathered his resolve.
uncertainty_note: The final verb is pale; жыйылып is the best visual reading and English is contextual.

en: The son of Khan Suurchulgan,
uncertainty_note: The first word is a provisional proper-name reading; its joined middle letters are indistinct.

en: Who had come and stood here,
uncertainty_note: Бурада is the closest visual reading and may instead be a dialectal spelling or proper name; English is contextual.

en: Safe and sound, remaining upright,
He directed his people toward one course,
uncertainty_note: The word read жак is faint; translation follows the apparent idiom.

en: Arka Kongoz, the scourge of the foe,
uncertainty_note: Арка конгоз is a provisional reading, probably an epithet or name; English treats жоо күйүк contextually.

en: What he drove was different, on the returning day,
uncertainty_note: The middle word appears to be бөлөк and the final phrase кайра күн; the syntax and English remain provisional.

en: Do not ask about his waters,
uncertainty_note: The first word is visually close to Суусунун, but the intended idiom is unresolved.

en: He set straight whichever way he looked,
When he spoke, [the final phrase is uncertain],
uncertainty_note: Сөз сүйлөгөнү is clear; былкыл күл is a visual approximation whose sense is unresolved.
